survey: A stage spotlight hangs from a lighting truss. The truss is two parallel grey tubes joined by zigzag braces. It runs almost straight across the frame, rising slightly to the right, and is seen nearly front-on from a little below. A dark clamp wraps the truss at the top centre, and a bolt on the clamp holds a U-shaped yoke. The yoke's crossbar is level and its two arms hang straight down. Each arm ends in a round pivot hub on one side of the lamp. The lamp is a cylinder turned in three-quarter view, aimed down and to the left toward the viewer. Its back upper surface, with three vent slots, faces the camera, and an orange band circles its middle. The front face is an ellipse holding three round lenses (yellow, cyan, red), which narrow about as much as the front rim does. Coloured light beams spread down-left from the lenses. Overall the truss, clamp, lamp body, band and lenses agree on one camera. The lenses and band follow the cylinder's turn, and the truss tubes stay roughly parallel with only mild stylised convergence.

errors.where: Yoke pivot hubs on the sides of the lamp cylinder
errors.what: The two pivots don't sit on one cross-section of the cylinder. The left hub is at the front rim, ahead of the orange band, while the right hub is well behind the band toward the back. A line through the two hubs is nearly level, but the cylinder's cross-sections (shown by the band) run steeply down to the right. So the hubs aren't opposite ends of one axis at right angles to the lamp body, and the yoke reads as flat to the picture while the lamp is turned three-quarter.

fix: Attach the U-shaped yoke to the lamp at two pivot hubs exactly opposite each other on the same cross-section of the cylinder, both level with the orange band. Turn the yoke with the lamp so its arms sit on either side of the cylinder at the band. Keep the truss, clamp and lamp seen from one consistent camera.
